findings.summary: Some sample-based figures in the new tables do not hold over larger uniform row samples, e.g. 0 rejected on causal rows at N = 4096: README 4-5%, three 128-row samples 1.7-1.9%
findings.detail: The README's figures come from 24 sampled rows, over two samplings. I re-evaluated Model.lean's new formulas on 128 rows spread evenly over the head (every row at N = 128, every 8th at 1024, every 32nd at 4096), three seeds (work/tol_uniform.out). Most figures agree. These do not: (1) Share of elements where Post rejects 0, test data, causal rows: README 7-8% at N = 1024 and 4-5% at 4096 (table 'Where Post does not tell o from 0': 0 meets Post on 91.5-92.6% and 95.4-95.8%). Mine is 5.0-6.6% and 1.7-1.9% (0 meets Post on 93.4-95.0% and 98.1-98.3%). At N = 128 causal, D = 128, README 40%, mine 35-38.5%. (2) Benchmark at N = 1024, D = 128, non-causal: tolO median README 1.4-1.6, mine 1.16-1.49; Post rejects 0 on README 16-20%, mine 9.5-18.6%. D = 64 non-causal: README 50-54%, mine 45-57%. (3) Benchmark pE maxima: README 'at most 1.43' (D = 64) and 'at most 3.1' (D = 128); mine 1.46-1.65 and 3.05-3.62. Medians agree (1.31-1.32 and 2.18-2.36). The differences overstate slightly how often Post rejects 0, and none changes a conclusion. To resolve: give these figures from larger, evenly spread row samples, or widen the ranges to cover them and say they are from small samples.
findings.evidence: work/tol.py ('python3 -I tol.py uniform'), work/tol_uniform.out; work/tol.out (python3 -I tol.py: rows 0-63 and N/2 to N/2+63, which over-weights early causal rows, so its causal shares are not uniform-sample figures).

notes: Re-review after library round 24 (L124, L125), gate 4740b3814ba92693. assumption:dot now cites DotE5m2Chunk, which is the library's fact for both fp8 tl.dots (float8e5 x float8e5 into float32, maxImpreciseAcc = 2^30, any precision; num.md's row and Dot8Chunk.lean). The other assumptions re-opened only because num.md and Sm90.lean changed. Exp2F32, Exp2F32NegInf, Log2F32 and CvtSatF32E5m2 are unchanged in Sm90.lean, and DivFull, DivTotal, MathTotal, CvtTotal and DotTotal keep their rows, so I accept all of them again. The new spec's names (scoreLift, scoreErr, HeadOk, scoreE, blkLW, accNext, errNext, tolO, iotaV, magCp, Post) print as kernel, TVA or Mathlib definitions (work/print_spec.lean, print_spec.out). main, consistent and satisfiable use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. scoreErr is Dot8Chunk.errB over the q.k chunks, which is DotF8Chunk.err's bound from a zero accumulator, as line 73 uses it. Over every test_op shape and the benchmark at N = 1024, Model.lean's new formulas (work/tol.out, tol_uniform.out) reproduce the README's tolO, tolV and tolM medians and the v = 1, one-key and vEff = 0 rows: v = 1 gives tolO 0.463 / 1.31 / 19.3 / 1.17e6 and tolV 0.658 / 2.67 / 80.6 / 1.86e7; one key gives 0.31-0.33 |attnRef|. The exceptions are in the DOC finding. Heads without vIn stay pinned: tolV at K = R = 0 is 7.63e-6 < 2^-16 at every covered size, iotaV = 0 removing liftMag's 2^-14, so o = ±0. HeadOk's new cap covers the host: the largest sigma*scoreLift I sampled is 16.7 (test, D = 128, cap 256) and 168 (benchmark, N = 1024, D = 128, cap 256). The lift adds at most 2^-14*sigma*sum(|q| + |k| + 2^-14), about 0.02, to round 1's 184-196 at N = 2^14. The tightening is real. On the benchmark, tolO goes from 13.9 / 1.2e4 to about 0.55 / 1.2-1.5, and Post now rejects 0 on 10-69% of the elements. On the test's data, tolO is 1.8-5.5x the fp8 floor.
